title: Throughput Governor Inspector — UI for adjustable throughput controls and change playback
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Operators managing Dedicated fleets need a single inspector to understand and adjust throughput guarantees, view the effective autoscaling policy that will act on a fleet, and replay or rollback recent control plane changes. Current console screens are scattered: scaling presets live in one panel, throughput time-series in another, and the change log is a separate audit timeline. This causes cognitive overhead and slows incident responses.

Goal: Build a Throughput Governor Inspector (TGI) panel in the Console Fleet Controls surface that consolidates: (1) adjustable throughput controls (target RPS, burst allowance, available headroom), (2) a small, actionable autoscaling policy summary (min/max/scale-step/queue thresholds), (3) a throughput and utilization dashboard with 1m/5m/15m rollups and predicted short-term capacity, and (4) an ordered change history with playback and safe-rollback actions.

Success metrics: reduce mean time to resolution for capacity incidents by 30% (measured on demo fleets), 25% fewer manual scale-up escalations over a quarter, and 90% of operators report the TGI reduces context switching in usability study.

Constraints & non-functional requirements: changes made through TGI must go through an approval/workflow for enterprise customers (Respect role-based operations), actions must be auditable (append immutable entry to audit log), real-time telemetry must be rate-limited to avoid billing spikes for very large fleets, and UI experiments must support a canary toggle to expose the inspector to 10% of accounts initially.

Proposed UX: left column shows current throughput target and quick-adjust controls (preset sliders + numeric entry + "apply with preview"), middle column shows a stacked time-series (requests, served tokens, queue depth, p95 latency) with a 30m prediction band, right column shows current autoscale policy in human-readable rules and the recent change list (with author, timestamp, reason, diff). Each change entry supports: view diff, preview effect on prediction, revert, or create a rollback playbook that will schedule a controlled rollback.

Acceptance criteria: (1) TGI panel reachable from Fleet Controls > Inspectors, (2) can update throughput target and persist change to the control plane with appropriate audit entry, (3) autoscale policy summary reflects live config and shows which rule matched last scale event, (4) change playback shows a time-aligned simulation of effect, and (5) QA signoff on role gating and audit entries.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Initial PM briefed Eng and Design. Agreed to scope UI-only controls first, backend hooks to be added in follow-up sprint.
2025-02-12 — Design (Nina Park) uploaded wireframes to Figma: https://figma.redwood.ai/file/TGI-wires. Requested: compact diff view and 'preview on sample fleet' button.
2025-02-13 — ENG tech spike (ENG-19382) completed. Findings: can reuse kube-based rollout metadata for the change history; need an API to compute short-term capacity prediction (estimated 2 sprints).
2025-02-14 — Security review triage: no new data flows; enterprise RBAC mapping required. Security assigned follow-up ticket ENG-20105.
2025-02-16 — PM review with Customer Success: suggested adding 'impact estimate' per change (e.g., expected latency delta). Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-18 — UX review notes: reduce noise in time-series by defaulting to 5m rollup. Design to deliver hi-fi mockups by 2025-02-21.
2025-02-18 — Ready for Eng PR and API contract. Linked artifacts below.
notes: We should prioritize a read-only preview mode for SREs so they can simulate 'what-if' without write permission. Consider adding lightweight ML model for short-term capacity prediction, but scope the ML work to a follow-up. Coordinate rollout with Customer Success for 3 pilot accounts.
